guardian.title: Archaeologists uncover ancient Byzantine city in Egypt’s western desert
guardian.description:
Well-preserved fourth-century quarters reveal details of daily life, urban development and economic activities

Archaeologists in Egypt have uncovered a well-preserved Byzantine-era city in the western desert.

The fourth-century quarters had residential and religious structures, including a basilica-style church in the Dakhla oasis. Archaeologists also found coins, pottery fragments and tools.

El Obeid becomes key battleground in war between Sudan’s armed forces and their paramilitary enemies, the RSF

Fatima has lost count of the number of drone attacks on the besieged city of El Obeid in Sudan, but said the attacks this past weekend were the most violent so far.

A leading higher education programme, aimed at keeping 1 million girls in school across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, has been axed by the British government just two years after it was announced.

guardian.title: ‘Give him any award, and he’ll come running’: Narendra Modi racks up honours on overseas trips
guardian.description:
Indian prime minister has a habit of collecting awards on his travels, some as their first and only recipient

As Narendra Modi touched down in Seychelles over the weekend, the archipelago nation in the Indian Ocean swiftly bestowed one of its “highest” honours upon the Indian prime minister.

Modi beamed as he accepted the Guardian of the Blue Horizon award from Patrick Herminie, the Seychelles president, complete with a trophy and certificate.

guardian.title: Côte d’Ivoire floods kill 59 as west Africa endures torrential rains
guardian.description:
Authorities say rainy season getting deadlier, with Ghana reporting 13 dead and floods hitting Benin, Togo and Nigeria

Floods in Côte d’Ivoire have killed 59 people since May, the communication minister told a cabinet meeting in Abidjan.

There are fears the toll could further rise as rescue teams continue to search for victims during the rainy season, which runs from May until July, the minister, Amadou Coulibaly, added.

guardian.description:
Impoverished island was already struggling to keep the lights on before the US imposed a blockade in January

Cuba on Monday suffered its third nationwide power outage since the start of the year, the state electricity company said.

guardian.description:
TKMS beats South Korean rival to multibillion-dollar contract that will deepen Canada’s Nato ties

Canada has selected a German consortium to build a dozen cutting-edge submarines in one of the country’s largest-ever defence contracts that will further deepen its Nato ties before a crucial summit this week.

guardian.title: Cuban zoo celebrates birth of Bengal tigers amid energy crisis
guardian.description:
Arrival of endangered cats, including rare white cub, revitalises team straining under fuel and medicine shortages

For the Cuban zookeeper Ángel Cordero, the sight of four Bengal ⁠tiger cubs playing in a cage at the Cuban national zoo is a small miracle on an island stifled by shortages ⁠of fuel, medicine and ⁠days-long power outages.

The ​birth of these endangered big cats – including an exceedingly rare white tiger – has revitalised a team of zoo workers, he said.

guardian.title: Rodríguez defends Venezuela’s emergency earthquake response as number of bodies expected to soar
guardian.description:
Interim president says unrest will not break out despite anger at official response to the 24 June disaster

Venezuela’s interim president has defended her country’s emergency response to the twin earthquakes that have killed more than 3,000 people, vowing the country would not descend into social unrest.

Many Venezuelans have expressed anger at what they see as the US-backed government’s inadequate response to the 24 June disaster before international teams arrived.

guardian.description:
Tropical storm causes extreme flooding in south of the country with heavy rainfall expected in coming days

A tropical storm has killed two people, caused dam breaches and forced tens of thousands to evacuate in southern China.

Typhoon Maysak killed two people in Nanning, in China’s southern Guangxi province. Maysak, which lashed Vietnam and China’s southern island province of Hainan over the weekend, will dump the water it sucked up on its way ⁠across the South China Sea as it wea

guardian.title: China tests long-range missile in South Pacific in move Australia condemns as ‘destabilising to region’
guardian.description:
Launch comes just hours after Australia and Fiji sign defence agreement as expert says timing not a coincidence

China has conducted a long-range missile test in the South Pacific just hours after Australia signed a defence agreement with Fiji, sparking condemnation from Canberra and regional leaders.

guardian.description:
Ezra Jin, founder of Zion Church, lands in the US and reunites with family who are ‘overwhelmed with joy’

The founder of one of China’s most prominent underground churches has been released from prison and reunited with his family in the United States.

guardian.description:
Officers found body of 34-year-old man in luxury rental home in Pattaya area, local media says

A 21-year-old British woman has been arrested in Thailand after allegedly fatally stabbing her boyfriend, according to local media reports.

guardian.title: China says man who flew plane into Beijing skyscraper had mental health problems
guardian.description:
Official statement offers the most detailed official account yet of the highly unusual and fatal incident in Beijing

Chinese authorities said the man who flew a small plane into Beijing’s tallest skyscraper last week was a 66-year-old who had mental health problems.

The statement published on Thursday offered the most detailed official account yet of the highly unusual incident that occurred in Beijing’s central business district on the evening of 26 June.

rfi.title: NATO summit in Ankara tests unity as Ukraine war and Trump tensions loom
rfi.description: As NATO leaders gather in Ankara tomorrow, Tuesday, the alliance faces a stark test of unity, burden-sharing and strategic clarity, with the war in Ukraine, transatlantic tensions and Middle East instability all pressing heavily on the agenda.

rfi.title: France's first diagnosed Ebola patient recovers after treatment
rfi.description: A French doctor who was the first-ever diagnosed case of Ebola in the country has made a full recovery and has been discharged from hospital.

rfi.title: Major wildfires burn in Southern France as early fire season hits Europe
rfi.description: Firefighters are fighting wildfires across southern France and other parts of Europe, and authorities are warning that this year’s fire season has started a month earlier than usual after early heatwaves in May and June left vegetation particularly dry and vulnerable.

rfi.title: European football chiefs hit out at Fifa move to lift ban on US star Balgoun
rfi.description: European football's governing body Uefa on Monday lashed out at the decision of World Cup organisers Fifa to suspend the immediate one-match ban of the United States striker Folarin Balogun following the intervention of US President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: Macron to become first Western European leader to visit post-Assad Syria
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron ​will visit ‌Syria to discuss ways to ​strengthen bilateral ​relations and issues of ⁠mutual interest, ​the Syrian presidency has announced, in what would be the first visit by a Western European head of state since Ahmed al-Sharaa came to power following the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad in late 2024.

rfi.title: Rebels seize key-town of Anéfis as rebels tighten grip on northern Mali
rfi.description: Tuareg separatists and al-Qaeda affiliates appear to have secured control of a key town in northern Mali following a coordinated offensive by the rebels over the weekend. The Malian army and Russian mercenaries have been holed up in the key camp of Anéfis after the rebels launched their offensive on Saturday 4 July.

rfi.title: Tour de France bans spectators from third stage as fire burns in French Pyrenees
rfi.description: Spectators have been banned from the third stage of the Tour de France cycling race through the Pyrenees Monday, which will be adapted as a forest fire burns the area.

rfi.title: Tanzania protesters face heavy security, fear repeat of deadly election violence
rfi.description: Tanzanians planning to protest Tuesday against government repression are facing a heavy police presence and warnings from authorities, which recalls the mass killings that followed last October's disputed election.

rfi.title: England survive Azteca thriller to set up last eight showdown with Norway
rfi.description: England moved into a last eight clash with Norway after they beat Mexico 3-2 in a whirlwind game for the ages at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

rfi.title: Haaland's late strikes take Norway past Brazil to last eight for first time
rfi.description: Erling Haaland scored twice in the last 11 minutes to sweep Norway past Brazil into the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time.

rfi.title: Summit host Turkey eyes major weapons deals with NATO allies
rfi.description: Next week's NATO Summit in Ankara is expected to showcase Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s rising influence within the alliance, as he aims to use the gathering to overcome resistance to crucial arms deals and highlight the rapid growth of Turkey’s defence industry.

rfi.title: Three sons of Iran's slain leader Khamenei appear at funeral, not successor Mojtaba
rfi.description: Three sons of slain Iranian leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei prayed beside his coffin and those of four other family members on Sunday, but Mojtaba, the son who has succeeded him as Iran's supreme leader, ​did not make ‌an appearance.

rfi.title: World Cup bosses wipe out ban for US striker Balogun on eve of Belgium tie
rfi.description: World Cup organisers Fifa on Sunday suspended the one-match for Folarin Balogun for his red card during the United States' 2-0 victory in the last 32 over Bosnia and Herzegovina on 1 July.

rfi.title: France's richest man Bernard Arnault ordered to pay €22.5m in back taxes
rfi.description: Bernard Arnault, head of the luxury goods group LVMH, has been ordered to pay nearly €22.5 million in back taxes after a Paris appeals court overturned earlier rulings in his favour in a long-running dispute with the tax authorities.

rfi.title: From memes to political movement, India's 'Cockroach' party leads youth revolt
rfi.description: India's Cockroach Janata Party began life as a series of internet memes and has grown into a real-life movement, bringing together young people angry about unemployment and alleged exam fraud. What began five weeks ago as a satirical response to comments by India's chief justice has become a fast-growing campaign which now has political ambitions, even as observers question whether it can survive without more effective organisation.

rfi.title: The Afghan women farmers keeping their village alive
rfi.description: In a remote province of northeastern Afghanistan, women farmers are playing a vital role in their community's survival among the snow-capped mountains.

rfi.title: Hunger in northern Nigeria reaches worst levels in nearly a decade, WFP says
rfi.description: More than 17 million people across nine conflict-hit states in northern Nigeria face severe hunger, the UN's food agency (WFP) has said, warning that violence and funding ‌cuts are driving food insecurity to its worst level in nearly a decade. Stripped of their livelihoods, some people are fleeing across the border into neighbouring Benin.

rfi.title: Mbappé strikes to send France into last eight showdown with Morocco at World Cup
rfi.description: After a 1-0 win in Saturday's match against Paraguay, France will take on Morocco for the second consecutive World Cup. In 2022 in Qatar, they met to contest a place in the final. Four years later in the United States, they will play for a place in the semi-finals.

euronews.title: Artists create giant sea animals from sand
euronews.description: Artists create large sand sculptures of marine life on Rab island in Croatia during the Festival of Sand Sculptures, turning the beach into a temporary exhibition.

euronews.title: Pamplona's San Fermín festival begins with fireworks and celebrations
euronews.description: Thousands gather outside Pamplona City Hall as fireworks, music and dancing mark the official opening of Spain's San Fermin Festival.

euronews.title: Space debris on Queensland beach: 'space balls' washed ashore, do not touch
euronews.description: In Australia, authorities warn after several so-called space balls appeared on a beach in Queensland. Anyone who finds one must call emergency services at once and must not touch it.

euronews.title: Number of Portuguese nationals and people of Portuguese descent killed in Venezuela rises to 96
euronews.description: The number of Portuguese nationals and people of Portuguese origin killed in the twin quakes in Venezuela has risen to 96, the Foreign Ministry told Lusa.

euronews.title: Hungary could vote to oust president as early as next week as opposition complains of 'tyranny'
euronews.description: Viktor Orbán's Fidesz is calling for protests after Prime Minister Péter Magyar filed a constitutional amendment to remove President Tamás Sulyok.

euronews.title: Microsoft cuts 4,800 jobs with Xbox facing its biggest shake-up
euronews.description: About 3,200 gaming jobs are set to be cut at Xbox over the coming fiscal year.

euronews.description: Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have razed multiple villages in the western regions of the country bordering Chad, killing many and displacing thousands as a separate UN report outlines that over 300 children were killed in their atrocities this year alone.

euronews.title: European Commission renews pressure to open new accession cluster with Serbia
euronews.description: Commission pushes EU states to open Serbia's accession Cluster 3 in July, citing reform progress on foreign policy alignment, rule of law and electoral legislation. But the move is set to face opposition from the member states.

euronews.title: EXCLUSIVE: EU Commission and capitals headed for collision over Serbia's Cluster 3 negotiations
euronews.description: Brussels is seeking to revive Serbia's accession bid and could discuss as early as Wednesday its case for opening Cluster 3. But EU capitals remain divided over whether recent measures are enough to offset wider democratic backsliding.  For some, it's too much, too soon.

euronews.title: EU demands fairness and transparency after FIFA's Balogun reversal
euronews.description: "We support the principle of fair play and transparent competition," the European Commission said as fury at FIFA intensifies.

euronews.title: South Aegean bids for 2028 World Region of Gastronomy title
euronews.description: Greece’s island cuisine stands out for its quality, nutritional value and, of course, its irresistible flavour.

euronews.title: Ukraine hits vital oil refinery more than 2,500km behind Russian border
euronews.description: While Russia continues to pound Ukraine with missiles and drones, killing at least 19 people and injuring dozens more in Kyiv, Ukraine is striking deep inside Russian territory as part of a campaign to degrade the Kremlin’s war machine.

euronews.title: Green groups say EU-backed chemical alliance puts polluters first
euronews.description: A watchdog's report challenges the industry's claims that European chemical manufacturers are facing an existential crisis due to high energy costs and Chinese competition – one of the pillars of the European Commission's competitiveness pledge.

euronews.title: Italy tops European tourism in 2026 with a busy summer in sight
euronews.description: Visitor numbers increased during the first half of 2026, driven primarily by international tourists. Tourism Minister Mazzi said "The sector remains a pillar of the national economy."

euronews.title: Good breeding: Kazakh 'satin' horse becomes new national symbol
euronews.description: A very rare satin hair coloured horse called Aqzhal is widely being celebrated in Kazakhstan as a traditional symbol of prosperity and power.

euronews.title: Catania Airport suspends flights following volcanic activity at Mount Etna
euronews.description: Passengers are being urged to check their flight status, with some airlines being diverted to Palermo Airport.

euronews.description: Belgian fans said FIFA's decision to overturn Folarin Balogun's suspension was "not normal" ahead of Belgium's World Cup match against the United States.

euronews.title: UK sanctions Russian scientists and labs behind chemical attacks, foreign office says
euronews.description: The institutions hit were SC Signal, a Russian state scientific research institute and GNIII VM, the country's Scientific Research and Testing Institute for Military Medicine.

lemonde.title: La France bascule dans une nouvelle vague de chaleur caniculaire, avec des pics à 40 °C
lemonde.description: Provoquée par un anticyclone au large du Portugal et des îles britanniques, la chaleur s’est installée lundi dans une large partie du territoire, avec des valeurs allant jusqu’à 38 °C, voire 40 °C, dans le Sud-Ouest et le Languedoc. Le troisième épisode caniculaire de l’année s’annonce intense et durable, probablement autour d’une douzaine de jours.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Portugal - Espagne : qui de Cristiano Ronaldo ou Lamine Yamal va remporter le choc des huitièmes de finale ?
lemonde.description: Quelques jours après un seizième de finale épique face à la Croatie, Cristiano Ronaldo et ses coéquipiers retrouvent l’Espagne, championne d’Europe en titre.

lemonde.title: Tir de missile balistique par la Chine : une démonstration de force qui inquiète ses voisins du Pacifique
lemonde.description: Lundi 6 juillet, un sous-marin nucléaire chinois a tiré un missile stratégique équipé d’une tête inerte vers le Pacifique. Un geste dénoncé par l’Australie, le Japon et la Nouvelle-Zélande et qui intervient alors que Pékin multiplie les démonstrations de sa force nucléaire montante.

lemonde.title: Ankara, ville sous cloche à la veille du sommet de l’OTAN
lemonde.description: Afin d’accueillir le 36ᵉ sommet de l’Alliance atlantique, mardi et mercredi, un dispositif sécuritaire impressionnant boucle la capitale turque, où tout rassemblement public est interdit durant treize jours. L’ONG Human Rights Watch dénonce un « recours abusif aux lois antiterroristes pour procéder à des arrestations massives ».

lemonde.title: En Israël, le coup d’Etat juridique du gouvernement Nétanyahou face à la justice
lemonde.description: En annonçant qu’il ne se plierait pas à une décision de la Cour suprême, le premier ministre israélien s’attaque frontalement à la plus haute instance juridique, ouvrant une crise constitutionnelle dans le pays.

lemonde.title: Les ahmadis, parias du Pakistan : « Notre seule faute est d’appartenir à la communauté ahmadiste. Les fanatiques croient que nous tuer leur vaudra le paradis »
lemonde.description: Cette communauté musulmane, forte de 600 000 membres au « pays des purs », vit dans la hantise de son effacement. Persécutés, discriminés et victimes de violences depuis les années 1950, ses adeptes – officiellement « hérétiques » – sont désormais traqués jusque dans leur fief, la ville de Rabwah, au Pendjab.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi la cour d’appel de Versailles a décidé de relaxer Dominique Boutonnat, jugé pour agression sexuelle
lemonde.description: Dans leurs motivations, les magistrats prennent le contre-pied du jugement de première instance, qui avait condamné l’ex-président du Centre national du cinéma et de l’image animée à trois ans de prison, dont un an ferme.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Mark Rutte, le secrétaire général de l’OTAN, dénonce des attaques russes « indiscriminées »
lemonde.description: Le chef de l’Alliance atlantique a estimé que les bombardements russes sur Kiev et sa région dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi montrent que le président russe, Vladimir Poutine, « perd le contrôle en raison des succès de l’Ukraine sur le champ de bataille ». Ces frappes ont fait au moins 22 morts dans l’oblast de la capitale ukrainienne, selon le dernier bilan des autorités.

lemonde.title: Affaire des assistants parlementaires européens du FN : un dispositif inédit de communication pour la cour d’appel de Paris
lemonde.description: A la mi-mai, une magistrate a été nommée porte-parole de la juridiction, afin « d’accompagner » ses décisions « dans le débat public et médiatique, dans une démarche pédagogique ». Une initiative sans précédent, qui répond aux attaques contre la justice, après la décision de première instance qui avait condamné la patronne du Rassemblement national.

lemonde.title: Propreté à Paris : Emmanuel Grégoire présente sa méthode pour traiter 1 000 « points noirs »
lemonde.description: La ville va s’appuyer sur une étude de 2023 qui a recensé, avec l’aide des éboueurs parisiens, 1 412 de ces « points noirs », classés en « huit typologies ».

lemonde.title: Au sein de LR, le cas du général Gomart, révélateur des ambiguïtés de Bruno Retailleau
lemonde.description: L’eurodéputé français, dont les propos critiques envers la junte burkinabée ont servi de prétexte à une rupture avec Paris, est accusé par ses détracteurs de défendre une position prorusse auprès du patron du parti Les Républicains, alors qu’il est considéré comme un possible ministre de la défense « RN-compatible ».

lemonde.title: La motion de censure des écologistes contre l’« inaction climatique » du gouvernement Lecornu est rejetée par les députés
lemonde.description: Au total, 132 députés ont soutenu cette motion, ce qui ne suffit pas à atteindre la majorité de 289 voix nécessaires pour faire chuter le gouvernement.

lemonde.title: Tour de France 2026 : Tadej Pogacar et UAE Emirates XRG continuent de frustrer les échappés
lemonde.description: Après son équipier Isaac Del Toro, le vainqueur du Tour sortant s’est adjugé la troisième étape, lundi aux Angles (Pyrénées-Orientales). Au terme d’une journée qui fut une fois encore difficile pour les coureurs partis de loin, il endosse le maillot jaune.

lemonde.title: Cédric Jubillar a reconnu dans une lettre être à l’origine de la mort de sa femme, Delphine Aussaguel ; selon l’un de ses avocats, il « n’a jamais eu l’intention de tuer son épouse »
lemonde.description: M. Jubillar, condamné à trente ans de réclusion criminelle en octobre 2025, s’était, jusqu’ici, toujours dit innocent. Le corps de Delphine n’a pas été retrouvé.

lemonde.title: Comment Starlink a réussi à s’imposer en Afrique
lemonde.description: La firme du milliardaire américain Elon Musk propose désormais ses services dans 26 des 54 Etats africains. De nombreux pays, initialement réfractaires au fournisseur d’Internet par satellite, espèrent ainsi réduire leur fracture numérique dans les zones rurales enclavées.

lemonde.title: Mort d’Alexeï Navalny : Londres sanctionne sept personnes et deux instituts de recherche russes
lemonde.description: Sept personnes et deux instituts de recherche russes sont accusés de développer des armes chimiques ayant servi à empoisonner l’opposant russe en 2024 et une mère de famille britannique en 2018.

zeit.description: Die Fraktionen von Union und SPD haben Änderungsvorschläge am Regierungsentwurf des neuen Heizungsgesetzes beschlossen. Eine Klage könnte das Gesetz verzögern.

zeit.title: Nicht zu kaufen: Wirtschaftssenatorin Giffey verschenkt ihre Lieblingsrezepte
Fußball-WM: Senatorin aus Paraguay beschimpft Mbappé rassistisch
Landtagswahlen 2026: Und so taumelt das Land auf die größte politische Krise zu
zeit.description: Die AfD könnte in Sachsen-Anhalt gewinnen, die Merz-Regierung wird das nicht verhindern. Uns sollte klar sein, was das bedeutet: Der Widerstand muss aus der Mitte kommen.

zeit.title: Brandursache unklar: Wohnung in Kassel geht in Flammen auf - ein Todesopfer
Iran: Dieses Regime ist gegen das Leben
zeit.description: Die Islamische Republik verklärt Chameneis Tod zum Märtyrertum. Damit erschafft das Regime einen neuen nationalen Mythos. Und macht klar, wer sein größter Feind ist.

zeit.title: KI-Texterkennung: Finde den Fehler
zeit.description: Soll man künstliche Intelligenz benutzen, um künstliche Intelligenz als Autorin von Texten zu entlarven? Das kann nicht lange gut gehen.

zeit.title: Unfälle: Zwei Autofahrer bei Zusammenstoß schwer verletzt
Frida Kahlo in der Tate Modern: Du bist nicht allein mit deinen Fehlern
zeit.description: Sie gilt als eine der bekanntesten Künstlerinnen der Welt. In London fahndet nun eine Ausstellung nach dem Erfolgsgeheimnis der großartigen Frida Kahlo.

zeit.title: Kriminalität: Verdacht auf Sexualdelikt an Kind - Mann festgenommen
Karibik: Auf Kuba fällt erneut landesweit der Strom aus
zeit.description: Das Stromnetz auf der Karibikinsel Kuba ist erneut zusammengebrochen. Die Ursache ist unbekannt. In den vergangenen Monaten kam es häufig zu Ausfällen, teils tagelang.

france24fr.title: Iran : marée humaine à Téhéran en hommage à Ali Khamenei
france24fr.description: ⁠Une foule d'Iraniens a défilé ⁠dans les rues de ​Téhéran lundi  lors d'un cortège funèbre en l'honneur de l'ayatollah Ali Khamenei, le dirigeant assassiné fin février par les Etats-Unis ​et Israël, durant la journée la plus marquante d’une semaine de cérémonies commémoratives à grande échelle. Reportage de notre correspondant Reza Sayah.

france24fr.title: Le bilan de l'épidémie d'Ebola en RD Congo dépasse les 500 morts
france24fr.description: L'épidémie d'Ebola en République démocratique du Congo a fait plus de 500 morts, a annoncé lundi l'Organisation mondiale de la santé, citant des sources officielles congolaises. La 17ᵉ épidémie dans ce pays d'Afrique, déclarée officiellement le 15 mai, est causée par le virus Bundibugyo, pour lequel il n'existe ni vaccin ni traitement.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : dans les coulisses de l'opération américaine pour sauver le soldat Balogun
france24fr.description: La décision prise dimanche par la Fifa d'annuler la suspension pour un match du buteur star des États-Unis est intervenue après un coup de fil entre Donald Trump et le président de la fédération internationale de football, Gianni Infantino. Mais elle est aussi le résultat d’une opération de lobbying de plusieurs jours menée par l’administration américaine.

france24fr.title: Tour de France : Pogacar remporte la troisième étape aux Angles et s'empare du maillot jaune
france24fr.description: Tadej Pogacar a ​remporté ‌lundi la ⁠troisième ‌étape du Tour ⁠de France, longue de ​195,9 kilomètres, ‌entre Granollers (Espagne) et Les Angles (Pyrénées-Orientales), ‌devant le Danois ​Jonas Vingegaard. Grâce à cette victoire, le Slovène ​prend la tête du classement général.

france24fr.title: Trump confirme avoir demandé à la Fifa un réexamen du carton rouge de Balogun
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a confirmé lundi avoir appelé le président de la Fifa Gianni Infantino pour demander un réexamen du carton rouge infligé à l'attaquant américain Folarin Balogun, afin qu'il puisse participer au match contre la Belgique.

france24fr.title: Syrie : lent rebond de l'économie après la levée des sanctions internationales
france24fr.description: La Syrie sort épuisée d'une longue guerre civile, à laquelle la prise du pouvoir en décembre 2024 par une coalition islamiste a mis fin. Depuis, les autorités s'emploient à réunifier le pays morcelé par le conflit et à rebâtir ses institutions. Sur la route menant de l'aéroport à Damas, les drapeaux français et syriens flottent côte à côte, dans l'attente de la visite du président Emmanuel Macron dont des Syriens espèrent des retombées économiques pour leur pays dévasté.

france24fr.title: "J'aurais voulu mourir à sa place" : les adieux des partisans d'Ali Khamenei à leur Guide
france24fr.description: Au son des slogans à la gloire du défunt Ali Khamenei scandés par la foule de ses partisans, Téhéran, où le deuil se mêle à la colère, vit au rythme des funérailles nationales de l’ancien Guide suprême.

france24fr.title: Pyrénées-Orientales : 700 pompiers mobilisés, le feu n'est pas fixé
france24fr.description: Toujours pas fixé, l'incendie dans les Pyrénées-Orientales, qui a entraîné l'évacuation de 10.000 personnes et chamboulé l'arrivée de l'étape du Tour de France, a provoqué d'importants dégâts lundi et les conditions météo compliquent la tâche des 750 pompiers à l'oeuvre.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : Damas, un soutien fiable pour Beyrouth ?
france24fr.description: Serge Berberi, notre correspondant à Beyrouth, analyse la situation.

france24fr.title: L'Assemblée rejette la motion de censure écologiste dénonçant la gestion de la canicule
france24fr.description: L'Assemblée nationale ⁠a massivement rejeté lundi ​une motion de censure des Écologistes, soutenus par La France insoumise. Ses auteurs ​dénonçaient une mauvaise gestion par le gouvernement des épisodes de canicule qui ont récemment touché la France. En plein débat interne au PS, son secrétaire général, Olivier Faure, a voté la censure à rebours de la majorité du groupe.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : Trump remercie la Fifa d'avoir suspendu le carton rouge à Balogun
france24fr.description: Cédric Ferreira, notre envoyé spécial à New-York, analyse la situation.

france24fr.title: Etats-Unis : les interférences de Donald Trump lors de la Coupe du monde 2026
france24fr.description: Matthieu Mabin, notre correspondant à Washington D.C., décrypte la situation.

france24fr.title: Double séisme au Venezuela : la solidarité s'organise à Catia La Mar
france24fr.description: Au Venezuela, le double séisme du 24 juin a fait au moins 3 342 morts, selon un décompte encore provisoire. Sur le littoral caribéen, la région la plus touchée, les rescapés et les bénévoles venus de tout le pays s'organisent entre eux pour se soigner, s'abriter, se retrouver. Reportage de Pascale Mariani et Maxime Pluvinet

france24fr.title: France : la justice rendra-t-elle Marine Le Pen inéligible en 2027 ?
france24fr.description: Mardi, Marine Le Pen saura si elle peut concourir une quatrième fois à la présidentielle : une peine de plus de deux ans d'inéligibilité prononcée la conduirait à devoir céder la place à Jordan Bardella.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Algérie : une abstention historique, le FLN en tête
france24fr.description: Le taux de participation des législatives du 2 juillet en Algérie s'est établi à 21,24 %, selon des résultats provisoires rendus publics lundi. Le Front de libération nationale arrive en tête du scrutin.

france24fr.title: Emmanuel Macron attendu en Syrie pour une visite historique affirme Damas
france24fr.description: Ziad Majed, professeur d'études sur le Moyen et Proche-Orient à l'Université Américaine à Paris, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : pour l'UEFA et Blatter, la Fifa dépasse les bornes
france24fr.description: L'UEFA condamne avec des mots forts la décision de la Fifa d'alléger la peine de l'attaquant américain Folarin Balogun dans un communiqué lundi. L'ancien président de la fédération fustige quant à lui la "relation" qui unit Donald Trump à l'actuel chef de la Fifa, Gianni Infantino. Le joueur de la team USA devrait être présent au coup d'envoi du match mardi à 2 h du matin.

france24fr.title: Les incontournables du Festival d’Avignon 2026
france24fr.description: Une majorité de femmes à la mise en scène des spectacles du "IN", la langue coréenne à l’honneur, des créations monumentales… La 80e édition du Festival d’Avignon marque un tournant ! Dans cette émission spéciale, nous vous emmenons au cœur de l'un des plus grands rendez-vous du spectacle vivant. Nous recevrons notamment le codirecteur du Festival, Raymond Yana. Focus aussi sur la fête du festival "OFF" pour sa 60e édition.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: Marco Rubio befürwortet Aufhebung von Baloguns Sperre +++ enatorin aus Paraguay beschimpft Mbappé rassistisch
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: So haben sich die Europäer vorbereitet, um einen Eklat zu verhindern
nzz.description: Die Verteidigungsallianz hat turbulente Monate hinter sich. In Ankara steht ein entscheidendes Treffen an. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Die Fifa hebt die Spielsperre gegen den besten amerikanischen Stürmer auf – Trump bestätigt Infantino-Telefonat, Belgien und die Uefa protestieren vergeblich
nzz.description: Folarin Balogun erhielt für den Achtelfinal eine Spielsperre. Trotzdem kann er gegen Belgien auflaufen. Die Fifa treibt ein unrühmliches Spiel mit den eigenen Regeln.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Über 30 Grad im Schulzimmer – aber die Klimaanlage gilt noch immer als Sündenfall
nzz.description: Bäume, Schatten und entsiegelte Pausenplätze sind erwünscht. Aber wenn Klassenzimmer überhitzen, braucht es mehr als grüne Symbolpolitik.

nzz.title: Eklat im Zürcher Ratssaal: Grüner zieht Nazi-Vergleich – ausgerechnet in einer Debatte über Hassrede
nzz.description: Anstatt Harmonie gibt es im Kantonsparlament Buhrufe und mahnende Worte der Ratspräsidentin. Besonders unrecht ist das der Grünliberalen Chantal Galladé.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Temperaturrekorde, Todesfälle und Waldbrände: Eine Hitzewelle belastet Europa
nzz.description: Der Sommer 2026 bringt weiten Teilen Europas eine Hitzewelle. Viele Länder melden Temperaturrekorde, tropische Nächte und zahlreiche hitzebedingte Todesfälle. Die Feuerwehr bekämpft Waldbrände in Frankreich und Griechenland.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Trumps zweite Amtszeit: Der US-Präsident lanciert Konten für Neugeborene
nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Manche AfD-Kritiker wähnen sich im Endkampf gegen Faschismus und relativieren Gewalt gegen missliebige Journalisten. Dieses Denken ist totalitär
nzz.description: Je weniger erfolgreich der Kampf gegen die AfD ist, desto wahlloser wird die Jagd auf vermeintliche Faschisten. Einigen ist das gleichgültig. Das zeigt: Teile der Linken haben sich aus dem demokratischen Diskurs verabschiedet.

nzz.title: Tour de France: Pogacar gewinnt die erste Pyrenäen-Etappe und nimmt Vingegaard das gelbe Trikot ab
nzz.description: Für die Veloprofis geht es nach dem Auftakt in Spanien nach Frankreich. Der Slowene lässt sein Team arbeiten und belohnt sich am Ende.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: 17 Tote in und um Kiew – Russland fliegt neue Luftangriffe auf Ukraine
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die jüngsten Entwicklungen des Ukraine-Krieges in Bildern
nzz.description: Die russische Invasion hat Millionen von Ukrainerinnen und Ukrainern in die Flucht getrieben. Während der Abnutzungskrieg unerbittlich weitergeht, droht Kiew durch die aussenpolitische Neuausrichtung von US-Präsident Donald Trump weiter unter Druck zu geraten. Die aktuellen Entwicklungen in Bildern.

nzz.title: Ein toter Inder soll nach 30 Jahren aus der Todeszone des Mount Everest geborgen werden. Das ist aufwendig, teuer – und sehr gefährlich
nzz.description: Dorje Morup alias «Green Boots» gilt als bekannteste Leiche des Mount Everest. Der Tote war jahrelang eine Wegmarke für Bergsteiger. Nun will ihn Indien zurückholen.

nzz.title: Absturzgefahr für Seilbahnen: Projekte zur Verkehrsentlastung der Städte haben es schwer
nzz.description: In Luzern sollen die Touristen statt in Reisecars mit einer innerstädtischen Luftseilbahn anreisen. Das Projekt hat einen schweren Stand, wie gescheiterte Projekte in anderen Städten zeigen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Aufgehobene Sperre nach Trump-Anruf: Politische Interventionen sind für den Fussball brandgefährlich
nzz.description: Nach Druck aus Washington schwächte die Fifa die Sanktion gegen einen US-Stürmer ab. Das hätte sie nicht tun sollen: Das Spiel lebt davon, dass für alle Mannschaften dieselben Regeln gelten.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Microsoft streicht Tausende Jobs bei Xbox +++ Arbeitslosenquote in der Schweiz sinkt im Juni auf 2,9 Prozent

observador.title: Reinventar o imobiliário com criatividade e storytelling
observador.description: A Dils aposta na criatividade e na construção de marca. Marta Silva Carvalho explica como o storytelling e a cultura estão a transformar o imobiliário.

observador.title: Hamas anuncia retirada do poder na Faixa de Gaza
observador.description: O Hamas demitiu o comité que governava Gaza e transferiu a autoridade para um organismo tecnocrático. O desarmamento, porém, continua fora de equação e Israel fala em "truque".

observador.title: "Força El Bicho". Um espanhol de coração dividido em Dallas
observador.description: Junto ao estádio de Dallas, a Rádio Observador encontrou um adepto espanhol que não fica chateado se Portugal vencer. "Sou muito fã de Ronaldo, gostava de o ver ganhar o Mundial".

observador.title: AMALIA. Entra em cena a IA portuguesa
observador.description: AMALIA foi oficialmente apresentado. É o primeiro grande modelo de IA focado no português europeu. Em código aberto, promete reforçar a soberania digital e impulsionar a inovação nacional no setor.

observador.title: Almada sem água. Como se justifica a crise de abastecimento
observador.description: Câmara de Almada criou gabinete de crise e garante estar a trabalhar em novos furos para restabelecer abastecimento a 100%. Várias localidades continuam sem água e sem previsão para a reposição.

observador.title: 180 dias de suspensão por assédio na Casa da Cultura
observador.description: O executivo municipal aprovou por unanimidade a sanção. O trabalhador agarrava e apalpava as vítimas por trás, em locais isolados, entre agosto de 2024 e dezembro de 2025.

observador.title: Avenidas Novas: buscas da PJ por denúncia "infundada"
observador.description: A PJ investigou contratos celebrados com duas empresas durante o mandato 2021-2025. A junta lisboeta rejeita as suspeitas e diz que a denúncia atentou contra o seu "bom nome".

observador.title: PS: promessa das 4.000 casas em Gaia está na "estaca zero"
observador.description: A vereação do PS na cidade acusa a autarquia de "manter um silêncio absoluto sobre a principal promessa" e de "inaugurar projetos e habitações que herdou de executivos socialistas".

observador.title: Lisboa revoga obra para corredor verde na Avenida de Ceuta
observador.description: Dez anos após ser apresentado, o projeto do corredor verde do Vale de Alcântara continua por concluir. A empreitada foi adjudicada em 2023 e a consignação nunca ocorreu.

observador.title: Quando chega finalmente o alívio? Temperaturas caem 11 graus
observador.description: É já a partir de quinta-feira que o país vai respirar um pouco de alívio com o ar fresco a entrar pelo Atlântico Norte e a acabar com esta onda de calor extremo. Quem vai sofrer, de novo, é a França.

observador.title: América: a suscitar inveja há 250 anos
observador.description: A propósito dos 250 anos decorridos após a independêncisa dos EUA, Alberto Gonçalves lembra a difícil relação da Europa com a América e os fundamentos do anti-americanismo

observador.title: O que o Campeonato do Mundo faz pela nossa saúde mental
observador.description: Praticar desporto faz bem à saúde. Mas apoiar uma equipa também. Sobretudo se for aquela que provoca arrepios ao som do hino nacional.

observador.title: Coimbra adjudica elaboração do novo Palácio da Justiça
observador.description: Câmara aprovou por unanimidade a adjudicação à empresa Vítor Hugo. Vereadora da oposição alertou para "preço anormalmente baixo" e exigiu acompanhamento.

observador.title: "Portugal é quem vende mais". Esgotam as bandeiras em Dallas
observador.description: Junto ao estádio de Dallas, antes do duelo ibérico, Luis vendia bandeiras de Portugal a 10 dólares. Esgotaram: "tinha 100 na mochila e ja me sobram poucas, vou vender tudo. Todos querem".

observador.title: Chega pede debate sobre falhas nos exames nacionais
observador.description: André Ventura anunciou pedido formal para debate na próxima semana, antes da discussão do Estado da Nação, e afasta para já comissão de inquérito.

observador.title: Autoridades procuram homem desaparecido em Viana do Castelo
observador.description: Alerta dado ao fim da tarde de domingo. Buscas no terreno rural e arredores contam com equipas cinotécnicas e Sapadores com duas viaturas.

observador.title: BE acusa Governo de colapso na avaliação digital de exames
observador.description: O deputado Fabian Figueiredo criticou a perda de confiança no modelo. Já o PS espera que o executivo assuma os erros, enquanto o PSD defende que a classificação digital não está em causa.

observador.title: Ligação elétrica entre Portugal e Marrocos "em cima da mesa"
observador.description: A ministra da Energia admite que mais interligações não evitam apagões, mas aceleram a recuperação. Portugal demorou entre 11 a 12 horas em abril de 2025.

spiegel.title: Kuba: Blackout und neue Signale an Donald Trump
spiegel.description: Während das gesamte Stromnetz auf Kuba erneut zusammengebrochen ist, signalisiert Raúl Castros Enkel Gesprächsbereitschaft gegenüber US-Präsident Donald Trump. Er gilt als enger Vertrauter seines Großvaters.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 heute: Das sollten Sie vor den Spielen am Abend und in der Nacht wissen
spiegel.description: Bestreitet Cristiano Ronaldo gegen Spanien das letzte Länderspiel seiner Karriere? Und: Wie gehen die USA mit der aufgehobenen Sperre von Folarin Balogun um? Alles Wichtige zu den Partien des Tages.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Sturz bei Sprung über Bande - Englands Jordan Henderson verpasst wohl Rest der WM
spiegel.description: Ein Freudensprung nach dem Sieg über Mexiko im Aztekenstadion ging bös aus: Der englische Mittelfeldspieler Jordan Henderson verletzte sich bei einem Hüpfer über die Werbebande am Arm. Er muss nach Medienberichten operiert werden.

spiegel.title: Elterngeld: Neuer Gesetzentwurf sieht offenbar drei statt vier Partnermonate vor
spiegel.description: Das Familienministerium will beim Elterngeld sparen und Väter mehr in die Pflicht nehmen – nur offenbar weniger als ursprünglich geplant. Ein Bericht zitiert aus einem neuen Gesetzentwurf.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Schwere russische Angriffe vor Nato-Gipfel gemeldet
spiegel.description: Einen Tag vor dem Nato-Gipfel in Ankara greift Russland die Ukraine erneut massiv an. Mehrere Menschen sterben. Präsident Selenskyj appelliert an die Verbündeten und erhebt schwere Vorwürfe gegen Kremlchef Putin.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Menschenrechtlerin kritisiert Verhaftungswelle vor Nato-Gipfel
spiegel.description: Die Menschenrechtsexpertin Emma Sinclair-Webb sieht in der Verhaftungswelle vor dem Nato-Gipfel in der Türkei eine neue Eskalationsstufe. Hier erzählt sie, weshalb die Regierung auch Satire fürchtet.

spiegel.title: Gaza: Hamas will Verwaltung an Technokraten übergeben
spiegel.description: Der Schritt ist Teil des von US-Präsident Donald Trump vorgeschlagenen Nachkriegsplans für den Gazastreifen: Die Hamas kündigt an, die Verwaltung des Gebiets an ein Gremium palästinensischer Technokraten zu übergeben. Sie stellt jedoch Bedingungen.

spiegel.title: Haushalt 2027: Wo Lars Klingbeil die Milliarden herholt
spiegel.description: »Wir schaffen das, woran die letzte Regierung gescheitert ist«, verspricht Lars Klingbeil. Doch um den neuen Haushalt zusammenzubekommen, braucht der Finanzminister riskante Manöver. Die wichtigsten Grafiken zum Etat.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Audi rammt Tunnelwand auf der A111 – Mann in Haft
spiegel.description: In einem Berliner Autobahntunnel kracht ein Audi mehrfach gegen die Wand, die Polizei greift die drei mutmaßlichen Insassen auf. Einer der Männer muss in Haft, wegen eines anderen Vorfalls.

spiegel.title: Taylor Swift und Travis Kelce: Wie Nutzer mit Fake-Hochzeitsbildern von Taylor Swift viral gehen
spiegel.description: Bislang gibt es keine Hochzeitsfotos von Taylor Swift und Travis Kelce. Trotzdem erhalten KI-Bilder des Paars im Netz Millionen Likes. Ist den Fans egal, dass sie eine Illusion sehen?

spiegel.title: Menschenhandel: Interpol nimmt 1024 Personen fest
spiegel.description: Prostitution, Zwangsarbeit und Kriminalität: Bei einem Schlag gegen Menschenhandel hat Interpol mehr als tausend Menschen festgenommen. Unter den Opfern der Verdächtigen sind auch Minderjährige.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Infantino tut so, als sei der Fall Balogun ein ganz normaler Vorgang
spiegel.description: Donald Trump hat bestätigt, mit Gianni Infantino wegen der Roten Karte Kontakt gehabt zu haben. Auch der Fifa-Präsident hat sich nun geäußert. Und: Folarin Balogun darf spielen. Alles Wichtige des WM-Tages zum Nachlesen.

spiegel.title: Rüstung: Benjamin Netanjahu warnt vor Kampfjet-Deal zwischen USA und Türkei
spiegel.description: Vor dem Nato-Gipfel gibt sich der israelische Ministerpräsident Benjamin Netanyahu alarmiert wegen eines möglichen Rüstungsdeals zwischen Washington und Ankara. Er sorgt sich um das »Kräftegleichgewicht im Nahen Osten«.

spiegel.title: Tour de France: Tadej Pogačar gewinnt vor Jonas Vingegaard das Fahrradbrennen
spiegel.description: In den Pyrenäen wüten Brände, Zehntausende Menschen müssen ihre Dörfer verlassen. Die Tour de France rollt trotzdem durch Berge und Wälder. Am Ende bewahrt Tadej Pogačar einen kühlen Kopf.

spiegel.title: »Deadly Patient«: Amazon löscht vergurkte KI-Synchro
spiegel.description: Die Dialoge waren hölzern bis unfreiwillig komisch: Amazon Prime hat den mittels KI synchronisierten Film »Deadly Patient« von der Plattform genommen.

spiegel.title: Neuwagen: Erweiterter Notbremsassistent soll auch Fußgänger und Radfahrer schützen
spiegel.description: Ab Dienstag müssen alle neu zugelassenen Pkw mit erweiterten Assistenzsystemen ausgerüstet sein. Sie sollen die Sicherheit von Menschen auf den Straßen deutlich verbessern.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn plant Megareserve für Brenner-Nordzulauf
spiegel.description: Österreich und Italien bauen ein Mega-Bahnprojekt durch die Alpen, auf deutscher Seite fehlt noch die Anbindung. Dafür legt die Deutsche Bahn weitere Milliarden Euro zurück. Bald soll der Bundestag entscheiden.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Donald Trump, Fußball-WM, Nato-Gipfel, Haushaltsentwurf von Lars Klingbeil
spiegel.description: Trump greift als Hobby-Schiedsrichter in die Fußball-WM ein und brüskiert danach Italiens Ministerpräsidentin Meloni. Immerhin: Klingbeils Haushaltsentwurf hat er noch nicht kommentiert. Das ist die Lage am Montagabend.

letemps.title: Dans les Pyrénées, le Tour de France éprouve ses premières restrictions liées au réchauffement climatique
letemps.description:
La troisième étape, remportée lundi par Tadej Pogačar, s’est déroulée presque à huis clos, en raison d’un mégafeu qui sévissait dans la région. Reportage dans les rues presque désertes, mais solidaires du drame, du village d’Angoustrine

phys-org.title: Did elephant energetics decide Hannibal's Alpine crossing route?
phys-org.description: A new analysis sheds light on the most likely route for the Carthaginian general's famous crossing of the Alps. The study, led by the University of Oxford and iDiv/Friedrich Schiller University Jena, reveals that the Col de la Traversette would have been the least energy-intensive route. The findings have been published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

phys-org.title: Cave finds reveal modern humans and Neanderthals may have shared long-term cultural continuity
phys-org.description: Tens of thousands of years ago, Homo sapiens coexisted with Neanderthals, Homo neanderthalensis. Many of us living today carry a small amount of Neanderthal DNA, indicating that the two species may have shared much more than just the same land. Now, a breakthrough archaeological discovery has revealed that the two species did not merely cross paths: they possibly shared a common culture that spanned more than 20,000 years.

phys-org.title: Physics-informed AI could accelerate development of controlled-release drug patches, bandages
phys-org.description: Brown University researchers have developed a new artificial intelligence method for predicting the rate at which materials used in controlled drug-release systems release therapeutic agents. The new method could slash the development time for new therapeutic patches, bandages and implants.

phys-org.title: Bees reveal emotion-like reactions, from 'lip licking' to head shaking, in new videos
phys-org.description: New research proving bumblebees exhibit emotion-like behaviors—previously thought to exist only in mammalian species—has implications for how scientists understand the consciousness of insects.

phys-org.title: AI could hurt employers in race for top talent
phys-org.description: Companies embracing AI to recruit faster could be damaging their ability to compete for top talent, according to a major new study.

phys-org.title: Neighbors shape plant life more than expected, scientists find
phys-org.description: Scientists at Leiden University have discovered that plants are strongly influenced by their neighbors, not just above ground but also through hidden networks in the soil. Their findings challenge long-held ideas about how plants shape their environment and could help improve sustainable farming.

phys-org.title: First synthetic protein motor moves along DNA in controlled, programmable steps
phys-org.description: Researchers from UNSW Sydney have built the first artificial protein motor capable of taking controlled, directional steps along a DNA track. The protein, dubbed Tumbleweed, moves by alternating between three "feet" that bind to specific DNA sequences. By changing the surrounding chemical environment, the researchers can control both when the motor steps and the direction it travels.

phys-org.title: Algorithm determines which firms have advanced capabilities—and what others must build first
phys-org.description: Understanding how firms build their capabilities, such as managerial skills, technology adoption and innovation capacity, is important for explaining why some firms perform better and how others can improve. However, unlike sales or profits, firm capabilities are not easily quantifiable. So existing studies have used surveys or interviews to assess them, but these methods are costly, time-consuming and susceptible to bias.

phys-org.title: School-based program to reduce loneliness and improve help-seeking among adolescents
phys-org.description: Adolescents experiencing social isolation or loneliness are at increased risk of developing mental health problems, highlighting the need for preventive interventions before these challenges worsen. However, relatively few psychoeducational programs specifically address isolation and loneliness among adolescents, with most existing interventions focusing on individualized support.

phys-org.title: Four new groups of indigenous cacao varieties discovered in Peru
phys-org.description: A new genetic analysis of hundreds of cacao trees representing traditional Amazonian varieties grown on farms across Peru has revealed four previously unidentified, genetically distinct groups. Lambert Motilal, with colleagues from the Cocoa Research Center, The University of the West Indies, and Martha S. Calderon and Danilo E. Bustamante, with their colleagues from the Universidad Nacional Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza, partnered to explore Peru's untapped cacao diversity.

phys-org.title: Unexpected discovery yields new graphene oxide production method
phys-org.description: Researchers in the Texas A&M University J. Mike Walker '66 Department of Mechanical Engineering have developed a new method for producing graphene oxide, a high-value carbon nanomaterial used in batteries, electronics and advanced manufacturing.

phys-org.title: What do people really eat? New global database gives best answer yet
phys-org.description: A major new resource that provides one of the most comprehensive pictures yet of what people are eating around the world has been introduced in a new study by a UCL and University of Oxford researcher.

phys-org.title: Paleontologists make 'one in a million' discovery of soft tissue preserved in 450-million-year-old fossil
phys-org.description: Before the oldest dinosaur, before animals or even plants had expanded onto dry land, ancient relatives of starfish called crinoids, resembling stalked sea flowers, were among the first creatures to flourish in Earth's earliest coral reefs more than 450 million years ago. The study of fossilized crinoids helps scientists understand how these animals evolved and offers rare insight into the origins of complex life.

phys-org.title: Astronomers spot an extremely rare galaxy mega-merger
phys-org.description: Scale in the universe is hard to understand from a purely human perspective. Many times, the math just doesn't sit well with our brains, which evolved to capture and process data about the world around us rather than grok the complexities of stellar dynamics and galaxy mergers. But every once in a while, astronomers find something that, if we can wrap our heads around the numbers, gives a sense of just how big the universe is.

phys-org.title: Alpine butterflies track warming uphill, but habitat loss may pose bigger risk
phys-org.description: A new study published in the journal Alpine Entomology has found that alpine butterflies in the Swiss National Park are closely matching the pace of local warming in their range shift to higher elevations.

phys-org.title: Early parenting shapes the brain and socio-sexual behavior, rodent study shows
phys-org.description: Past psychology studies have consistently highlighted the importance of social bonds for survival, showing that enduring relationships are linked with a longer life expectancy, a more resilient immune system, better cardiovascular health and a lower risk of psychiatric conditions. In addition, they showed that being raised by two parents plays an important role in development, as it is often associated with better emotional regulation, cognitive performance and social competence in adulthood.

phys-org.title: Hidden fungal networks deliver carbon to green plants, experiment confirms
phys-org.description: Beneath forests, grasslands and wetlands lies a hidden underground network of fungi known as mycorrhizal networks, sometimes nicknamed the "wood-wide web." These fungi live in partnership with plant roots, helping plants absorb nutrients from the soil in exchange for carbon compounds produced through photosynthesis. These fungal connections can also link different neighboring plant species.

phys-org.title: Satellites reveal when toxic algal blooms flare in Blue Mesa Reservoir
phys-org.description: The summers of 2021 and 2022 were tough seasons for Colorado's Blue Mesa Reservoir. A severe drought gripped much of the western U.S., prompting emergency water releases that brought the reservoir to its lowest level since 1984. Marinas and boat ramps closed, remnants of a ghost town emerged from the muck, and parts of the reservoir turned greenish and swirled with toxic cyanobacteria blooms.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Acceptable Path for Designer Babies
proj-syn.description: Genetic-engineering tools with which to design one's progeny already exist, and they are being made even more potent with AI—at least for those who can afford such services. In the absence of policy interventions, we will be hurtling toward a tiered society in which economic privileges become biological advantages.

proj-syn.title: The Democratic Turkey NATO Needs
proj-syn.description: At NATO's upcoming summit in Ankara, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will seek to portray his country as stable, confident, and essential to Western security. But only the last one is true, which is why the restoration of democracy in Turkey is more than a domestic concern.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup as It Should Be
proj-syn.description: While Donald Trump was widely expected to lord over this year’s World Cup, which the United States is co-hosting with Mexico and Canada, it has turned out not to be his scene. National teams populated with immigrants, and small-town America’s embrace of the event, go against everything Trump’s MAGA movement stands for.

proj-syn.title: The Real Threat to NATO
proj-syn.description: The greatest challenge to NATO comes not from its adversaries but from within. As its leaders gather in Ankara on July 7-8, they should focus less on military capabilities than on reinvigorating the alliance's founding strategic philosophy, centered on democratic legitimacy, human rights, and the rule of law.

proj-syn.title: How the EU Can Lead the Rest of the West
proj-syn.description: While Europe is not just another middle power, nor is it a great power with sufficient economic, military, and geopolitical clout to dictate terms on the global stage. Instead, Europe is the ideal candidate to convene and lead a group of like-minded middle powers, not as a US-style hegemon, but as a first among equals.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Face the World on Its Own
proj-syn.description: Under pressure from Russian aggression—which has reached its full expression in the ongoing war against Ukraine—and an increasingly hostile US administration, Europe urgently needs to make progress toward a defense union. But that will require Franco-German leadership of the kind that is not yet on offer.

proj-syn.title: How Safe Are Today’s Blockbuster Tech Stocks?
proj-syn.description: Today’s wave of mega-IPOs has unleashed a wave of analogies to past booms. While no analogy is perfect, an especially apposite—and sobering—case may be what followed Nippon Telegraph and Telephone’s IPO in February 1987.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dolce Vita?
proj-syn.description: Glacial growth, aging welfare states, and a shortage of centrist leaders suggest Europe faces a major debt crisis in the years ahead. But its emphasis on leisure over work could become a decisive advantage, positioning the continent as the leading model for thriving in an age of AI-driven abundance.

proj-syn.title: The Putin Escalation Risk
proj-syn.description: If Ukraine can continue to disrupt Crimea, strike more targets in the heart of Russia, frustrate Russia’s frontline forces, and pile more pressure on Russia’s hobbled economy, President Vladimir Putin will feel increasingly cornered. The temptation to escape his predicament through a game-changing attack will grow stronger.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s New German Question
proj-syn.description: Without a EU-level framework capable of turning resources into scale, the bloc’s defense capabilities will remain limited, no matter how much member countries spends. If Germany, in particular, insists on going it alone, Europe could remain fully dependent on the US for key assets.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: 250 Years of American State Capitalism
proj-syn.description: While the prevailing economic narrative in the United States has often extolled free markets, policymaking itself has always been more pragmatic. From its very founding, the US has had a hybrid model in which the state directs, subsidizes, and occasionally bails out private enterprise in the service of national priorities.

proj-syn.title: Three Essentials of a More Equal World Order
proj-syn.description: A growing awareness of the inequities embedded in the world order has prompted calls for reform. Building a multilateral system that serves the global majority will require redesigning the international financial architecture, especially in relation to sovereign debt and corporate taxation.

proj-syn.title: The US as the World’s Robber Baron
proj-syn.description: Like the Gilded Age robber barons, the United States under President Donald Trump is using trade policy to benefit itself at the expense of all other countries. But now that administration surrogates are openly acknowledging the strategy, all other major trading powers will surely respond accordingly.

proj-syn.title: A Democratic Opening for Azerbaijan
proj-syn.description: With Armenia's recent elections likely to usher in an era of greater stability—and less Russian influence—in the South Caucasus, neighboring Azerbaijan is well-positioned to deepen cooperation with the US and Europe. But without appropriate conditions, new strategic partnerships with the West could fail to deliver for Azerbaijanis.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Europe’s Economy
proj-syn.description: While Nobel laureate economists Paul Krugman and Philippe Aghion disagree over how to measure Europe’s productivity gap with the United States, both overlook the value of its accumulated assets. That blind spot obscures the real story: Europe is living off a remarkable inheritance it has yet to convert into new growth.

proj-syn.title: NATO Needs a Defense Market
proj-syn.description: To convert NATO members' resources into military capabilities, setting defense as a strategic priority, increasing spending, and improving procurement systems are all steps in the right direction. But member countries will need to expand their industrial capacity—and that requires much more.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Choices Shaping our Children’s Health
proj-syn.description: Around the world, childhood is being reprogrammed by digital technologies that shape how young people learn, play, and connect. But children and young people are not experimental subjects, a captive market, or a commodity, which is why we must shape digital environments that protect and support their healthy development.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Cleantech Startup Funding Stabilizes As Energy Demand Grows
crunchbase.description: In the first half of this year, investors poured $15 billion into seed- through growth-stage rounds for companies in Crunchbase cleantech, EV and sustainability-focused categories. That puts funding on track to slightly exceed the 2025 tally, which was the lowest in several years.

crunchbase.title: A Year Of Misplaced Fear (And Why It’s Time For Investors To Leave The Crowd)
crunchbase.description: Many venture capital LPs have reacted to recent economic uncertainty by concentrating investments in megafunds, mistaking perceived safety for better returns while potentially sacrificing the higher upside that venture investing is meant to deliver. In this guest commentary, Sara Zulkosky,  co-founder and managing partner of Recast Capital, contends that smaller emerging VC managers are a more attractive source of long-term returns for investors willing to look beyond the crowd.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI, Energy And Biotech Lead The Way
crunchbase.description: U.S. startups announced sizable funding rounds at a steady clip during a truncated holiday week, with energy and AI leading the way. Houston-based energy startup Joulent secured the biggest round, a $1.75 billion strategic financing.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Global Startup Investment Hit Record $510B In H1 2026 As AI Boom Accelerates Funding And Exits
crunchbase.description: Investors poured more than $200 billion into startups globally in the just-ended quarter, making Q2 2026 the second-largest quarter on record, our data shows. And, with IPOs and acquisitions returning in force, the second quarter notched one of the strongest periods for venture-backed exits in years.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
crunchbase.description: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies were laid off in mass job cuts in 2025, per a Crunchbase News tally, and the layoffs have continued into 2026. See the latest companies to cut roles.

crunchbase.title: London-Based Tapestry VC Closes On $80M Third Fund To Invest In Repeat European Founders
crunchbase.description: Tapestry VC has closed an $80 million third fund to double down on Europe’s repeat founders and expects the coming wave of AI exits to produce yet another generation of experienced founders.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: No More Side Hustles: Why AI Startup Omnea Will Give Employees $250K To Openly Plan Their Next Startup
crunchbase.description: Omnea, a London-based artificial intelligence software company that helps businesses manage their supplier spending, is challenging traditional venture models with the launch of the Omnea Future Founders Fund to give its employees who have completed five years of service a chance to pitch for $250,000 in seed funding to launch their own companies.

crunchbase.title: We Need To Save Venture Capital From Bad Data
crunchbase.description: Venture capital firms are using AI the wrong way, argues Gilion's Henrik Landgren, who says that building better data infrastructure and connecting directly to sources like financial, payment and accounting systems would improve due diligence, help investors identify overlooked startups, and make investment decisions both faster and more accurate.

crunchbase.title: GV’s Dave Munichiello On Qualcomm’s Modular Purchase, The Firm’s 10x Return And The Shift In AI Software
crunchbase.description: The artificial intelligence space saw two major developments last week that highlight how technology companies are trying to manage the soaring costs and complexity of AI computing. In an interview with Crunchbase News, Dave Munichiello, a managing partner at GV, discusses the mechanics behind the Qualcomm-Modular deal, the practical realities of managing hardware scarcity, and what the current wave of consolidation means for the future of independent startups.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Q2 Brought The Most Billion-Dollar Startup Exits Since 2021
crunchbase.description: Startup exits valued at $1 billion or more are now more numerous than at any point since the 2021 market peak, Crunchbase data shows. The trend we’re seeing for the second quarter of 2026 includes both the largest venture-backed exit of all time and a bevy of other comparatively tinier but still sizable startup exits through acquisition or IPO.
